edges.description: Inactivation of the gene removes its protein product from the nucleus.
Loss of the tumour suppressor releases the restraint on chief cell proliferation.
Tumour growth produces the palpable mass.
Renal end-organ disease follows the sustained hypercalcaemia rather than the hormone directly.
Skeletal disease follows sustained PTH excess acting on bone.
A minority of invasive tumours go on to metastasise distantly.

edges.description: Reproduces Cdc73-driven parathyroid proliferation with raised serum calcium and PTH, which is the proximal mechanism this entry asserts.
edges.limitations: The tumours that develop are described as consistent with atypical parathyroid adenomas, not carcinoma, so the model captures the proliferative and hormonal arm of the mechanism and not the invasive behaviour that defines the human malignancy. It is a model of the germline HPT-JT lesion rather than of sporadic somatic disease, and the mice develop uterine neoplasms that are not part of this entry.

nodes.description: Absence of nuclear parafibromin immunoreactivity is the practical correlate of the genetic lesion, and the 2022 WHO classification gives the finding its own designation, parafibromin-deficient parathyroid neoplasm. The operating characteristics are asymmetric and the sources disagree on the specificity: one series reports 58% sensitivity with 100% specificity and loss confined to malignant tumours, while an earlier cohort found loss in 3 of 17 typical adenomas. The defensible reading is insensitive but highly specific, which is why a negative result does not exclude carcinoma and why diagnosis rests on the WHO invasion criteria rather than on this stain.
